S1.why: Like a shop tag ("2+1 δωρεάν"): the number plus δωρεάν, no noun, fits 12.

S2.why: An invitation in the polite plural imperative the vocabulary uses; "κι άλλα" is the spoken "more of them", so it reads as carrying on, not as a limit.

S3.s: Χρησιμοποιήσατε και τα %lld δωρεάν cutling. Μένουν δωρεάν και δουλεύουν όπως πάντα.
S3.back: You-used and the 5 free cutling. They-stay free and they-work as always.
S3.why: "και τα πέντε" is the Greek "all five"; cutling is the vocabulary's indeclinable item word, lowercase as in its iCloud sentence; δωρεάν is said twice on purpose because staying free is the point.

S4.why: States the allowance as a fact instead of "Μπορείτε να…" (you can), which a Greek screen would not open with.

S5.why: Same verb as S3; Greek keeps used-then-total order, so plain %lld twice; works for 1 because cutling does not decline.

S6.why: A noun phrase like the other bold row lines; Greek formats 5.000 with a dot, which arrives in %@.

S7.why: Uses the vocabulary's two kinds, Κείμενο and Εικόνες, in the plural, so the row does not invent "cutling εικόνων".

S8.why: Greek joins the last of three with και and no comma before it.

S9.s: Μία αγορά ισχύει σε κάθε συσκευή με τον λογαριασμό Apple σας.
S9.back: One purchase is-valid on every device with the account Apple your.
S9.why: "λογαριασμό Apple σας" and "κάθε συσκευή" are taken from the vocabulary's iCloud sentence; ισχύει is the plain word for a purchase that covers something.

S10.why: Plain present, polite plural; the everyday phrase, not the formal εφάπαξ, which the button carries instead.

S11.why: Greek negates a list with one χωρίς and ή; εγγραφή (sign-up) keeps λογαριασμός for the Apple Account only.

S12.why: The wording Greek iOS apps print for the App Store restore action, sentence case.

S13.why: The usual Greek in-progress form for a short action label, ending with the ellipsis character U+2026.

S14.why: A verbal noun, as Greek iOS buttons use; "4,99 € εφάπαξ" is how a Greek price tag says paid once. 21 characters before the price.

S15.why: The same verbal noun without the price.

S16.why: The phrase iOS in Greek uses for putting a prompt off without refusing it.

S17.why: The label Greek iOS gives its close buttons.

S18.why: "πια" carries the moment of change; spoken, warm, and covers the app and all the room at once.

S19.s: Ευχαριστώ για την αγορά. Στηρίζει το Cutling και τον άνθρωπο που το φτιάχνει.
S19.back: I-thank for the purchase. It-supports the Cutling and the person who it makes.
S19.why: Singular ευχαριστώ, because one person makes the app and a plural "we thank" would claim a team; the singular "τον άνθρωπο" says it is one person without spelling it out.

S20.s: Καλώς ξανάρθατε. Η αγορά σας επαναφέρθηκε.
S20.back: Well you-came-again. The purchase your was-restored.
S20.why: "Καλώς ξανάρθατε" is the native welcome back; επαναφέρθηκε matches the S12 action word.

S21.why: A spoken label, so a phrase with no verb; σε χρήση reads cleanly after any number.

S22.why: cutling does not decline, so the same sentence is right for 1, 2, 5 and 21; χώρο repeats the S6 word.

S23.s: Το Cutling ξεκλειδώθηκε. Χώρος για %@ cutling.
S23.back: The Cutling was-unlocked. Room for 5.000 cutling.
S23.why: Neuter article for the app as the vocabulary writes it ("Το Cutling"); the second sentence reuses S6 word for word.

S24.why: Passive with the purchase as subject, so no one is blamed; no full stop on an alert title.

S25.s: Δεν υπάρχει σύνδεση με το App Store αυτή τη στιγμή. Δοκιμάστε ξανά σε λίγο.
S25.back: Not there-is connection with the App Store this the moment. Try again in a-little.
S25.why: Names the cause, then the way out; "σε λίγο" is the spoken shortly.

S26.s: Το App Store δεν επιβεβαίωσε αυτή την αγορά.
S26.back: The App Store not confirmed this the purchase.
S26.why: One plain sentence with the App Store as subject, so the fault is not the person's.

S27.s: Δεν βρέθηκε αγορά του Cutling στον λογαριασμό Apple αυτής της συσκευής.
S27.back: Not was-found purchase of-the Cutling in-the account Apple of-this the device.
S27.why: "λογαριασμό Apple" as in the vocabulary; "βρέθηκε" (was found) already says the app looked for an earlier one, so "προηγούμενη" is left out to stay inside 80.

S28.s: Η δωρεάν έκδοση χωράει %lld cutling. Ξεκλειδώστε το Cutling μία φορά και αποθηκεύστε όσα θέλετε.
S28.back: The free version holds 5 cutling. Unlock the Cutling one time and save as-many-as you-want.
S28.why: χωράει is the spoken "holds" for room; the imperative pair says once-then-freely in the polite plural.

S29.why: The compact pair a Greek subtitle uses; the item word is already the list title above it.

K1.why: "τελείωσαν τα δωρεάν" is how Greek says a free allowance is used up (the items are not gone); "εδώ" tells the person to tap the capsule. 38 characters.

M1.why: Greek Mac commands and window titles are verbal nouns (Άνοιγμα, Κλείσιμο), so this is the native shape of a verb-led command.

M2.why: M1 with the ellipsis character because the button opens a window.

M3.why: The row label is the thing itself, with the vocabulary's item word.

M4.why: Greek settings write a count pair with από, not a slash.

M5.why: Neuter, agreeing with "το Cutling" named in the section header.

M6.s: Μία αγορά ξεκλειδώνει το Cutling σε iPhone, iPad και Mac.
M6.back: One purchase unlocks the Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: Same device list as S8; the purchase is the subject, as in S9.

M7.s: Ξεκλειδωμένο σε iPhone, iPad και Mac με αυτόν τον λογαριασμό Apple.
M7.back: Unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac with this the account Apple.
M7.why: Continues M5's neuter participle; "λογαριασμό Apple" as in the vocabulary.

M8.s: Αγοράσατε το Cutling πριν γίνει δωρεάν, οπότε μένει ξεκλειδωμένο. Σας ευχαριστώ.
M8.back: You-bought the Cutling before it-becomes free, so it-stays unlocked. You I-thank.
M8.why: οπότε is the spoken "so"; singular ευχαριστώ for the same reason as S19, with σας for the polite form.
